target_customer: Landowners and outdoor hospitality operators who host guests in off-grid units, plus event and disaster relief buyers
problem: Landowners lacked a fast, low cost way to add lodging; Jupe's flat-pack off-grid units assembled in about an hour with no permanent foundation and Jupe handled delivery, booking and cleaning.
business_model: Hardware sales or revenue share (about 30% of rental revenue per a 2023 interview) plus land partner services
product_category: Modular off-grid shelter hardware and outdoor hospitality

founders.name: Jeff Wilson
previous_startups: Kasita (modular tiny home, co-founder; described as having failed)
founders.background_notes: Styled Dr. in the press release, degree not stated. YC page also lists him as co-founder of No Cap (W23).

founders.name: Antonio Gonzalez
previous_startups: Led a $100 million sprinter van conversion business (per press release)
founders.background_notes: Per the press release he served on a presidentially appointed advisory board to the National Park Service.

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing a flat-pack, off-grid, solar and battery powered habitable unit with chassis mobility and manufacturing in California is hardware engineering well beyond software for a small team; product launched December 2020.

defensibility.rationale: Design and flat-pack shipping gave some edge, but tents, pods and prefab units were copyable and a 2023 interview says no outdoor hospitality player held more than about 5% of the market.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent moves against Jupe were found; no named competitor appears in the sources.

market_need_then: The 2021 press release cited demand from music festivals, disaster relief and remote lodging; the founder said the outdoor hospitality market was about $5 billion with no player above roughly 5% (2023 interview).

identity.visual_style: Space-inspired design; coverage described the product as inspired by 2001: A Space Odyssey
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline 'Just add land'; later positioned as a purpose built hospitality company

branding.community_and_virality: Wide design press at launch (Dezeen, Dwell, Business Insider, Yahoo) in December 2020 and early 2021.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong design press and a memorable tagline helped awareness and preorders, but no evidence of a community, merch or a brand-driven growth loop.

pivots.from: Pop-up shelter and disaster relief units
pivots.to: Short-stay-as-a-service land partner program for landowners
pivots.why: Business model described in the December 2021 press release; the company later describes itself as a purpose built hospitality company

outcome_analysis: Jupe raised a $9.5M seed in December 2021 after launching in December 2020, shipped dozens of units, and a 2023 interview projected about $12M revenue on roughly 400 deployed units. The YC directory marks it inactive, yet its website is live with a 2026 copyright, so the directory status conflicts with the evidence and no failure cause is recorded. Later ownership change claims are unverified.
notes: Status conflict: YC marks Jupe inactive but jupe.com is live (copyright 2026) and sells to outdoor hospitality, so exit type is unknown. A Simplify profile claims Jon Leonardo acquired Jupe in 2023; this rests on one low-detail aggregator and is unverified. Total funding in trackers ranges from $1.1M to $9.6M. The Feb 2021 angel round is mentioned in the 2023 Hampton interview with no amount or investors. Competitors: the PR release, TechCrunch article and Hampton interview name none; Veev appeared only on an aggregator and is not recorded. Dwell fetch was blocked (403) and not worked around. Name origin not found; a search returned unrelated results. Technical flag for Wilson and Gonzalez left null.
